title: Load a stage micrometer on a microscope, centre its crosshair and focus it sharply
instruction: Load the stage micrometer slide in the microscope's holder, label on the left, centre its crosshair in the field of view and focus its scale sharply.
context: Loading, centring and focusing a slide starts every microscope inspection. The holder snaps shut if let go, and focusing needs the coarse knob to get close without hitting the objective, then the fine knob to land within a 10 um depth of field.
setup: Station table (top 0.7475 m). Robot base frame: x forward, y to the robots' left. Upright microscope, fixed, facing the robots, centred at (0.34, 0.06): white stand with a 26 x 16 cm base, a pillar at the back and an arm over the stage carrying a steel 10x objective (24 mm across) on the axis (0.31, 0.06), front lens 12 cm above the table. Mechanical stage: dark plates (10 x 13 cm on top) that move up and down with the focus knobs and in x and y with the drive knobs; it starts 85 mm towards the robots (holder centre at (0.225, 0.06)) and 12 mm below focus. Slide holder on the stage: two back posts and a left stop, and a steel L-lever pivoting behind the slide's right end, its jaw across that end and its 9 cm handle out to the right with a black post (10 mm across, 2 cm tall) at the end; a light spring holds it closed. Drive knobs: two black ribbed knobs 34 mm across on a bracket out to the stage's front left, inner one (x drive) at (0.235, 0.165), outer one (y drive) at (0.235, 0.23), tops 9.5 cm above the table; they rise with the stage. Illuminator: a pale yellow spot of light 24 mm across on the objective's axis, shown on the slide (or the stage) under the objective; it rises with the stage. Focus: one shaft through a housing under the stage, with a black ribbed coarse knob 4.2 cm across on each side (axis 7 cm above the table at x = 0.30) and, outboard of each on the same axis, a fine knob 2.6 cm across and 1.2 cm wide. Stage micrometer slide, loose, 6 g: glass 76 x 26 mm (drawn 2 mm thick) with a black chrome crosshair 8 mm across, 10 mm right of centre, and a 1 mm scale in 10 um divisions along its x line; white label on the left end; it lies on a grey rest 1.6 x 6 x 3 cm at (0.18, 0.26), long side along y, label to the left.
scoring: Measured once everything has come to rest. 0 unless the slide is loaded: flat (tilt up to 3 degrees) in the holder with its centre within 3 mm of the holder's centre, label on the left (a slide turned end for end scores 0), holder jaw closed. 0 also if, once loaded, the slide came within 0.5 mm of the objective at any time. 0.25 if loaded; 0.5 if the crosshair's centre is also within 1.1 mm of the objective's axis (in the 2.2 mm field of view); 0.75 if the slide's top is also within 0.1 mm of focus (5.2 mm below the front lens); 1.0 if within 10 um of focus, the depth of field of the 10x / 0.25 objective. Real trial: the crosshair must be in the camera image at 10x; the focus error is the fine-knob travel needed to reach best focus of the 10 um divisions, read off its graduations.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Lower the stage 12 mm below focus, drive it 85 mm towards the robots and centre it left to right, take the slide out and lay it on its rest, label to the left.
fidelity: Rigid bodies in PhysX at 240 Hz. Knobs turn on damped hinges; the stage follows them through stiff drives, geared faster than a real stage (x 170, y 40 mm per turn, coarse focus 24, fine focus 1 mm per turn). The slide is drawn 2 mm thick (real 1 mm). No optics: focus is the stage height's distance from the focal plane, centring the crosshair's distance from the axis; the micrometer lines and light spot are drawn only.
